hints: Multiply z₁ and z₂ in exponential form by multiplying moduli and adding arguments.
Taking a conjugate preserves the modulus and changes the sign of the argument.
Write the conjugate of the product and factor its exponential into the separate conjugates, explicitly concluding the required equality.
walkthrough:
Write the product $z_1 z_2$ using exponent laws:
$$z_1 z_2 = \left(r_1\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\theta_1}\right)\left(r_2\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\theta_2}\right) = r_1 r_2\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}(\theta_1 + \theta_2)}$$

Take the complex conjugate of the product by negating the imaginary argument:
$$(z_1 z_2)^* = \left(r_1 r_2\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}(\theta_1 + \theta_2)}\right)^* = r_1 r_2\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}(\theta_1 + \theta_2)}$$

Express the individual conjugates $z_1^*$ and $z_2^*$:
$$z_1^* = r_1\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}\theta_1}, \quad z_2^* = r_2\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}\theta_2}$$

Multiply the individual conjugates together:
$$z_1^* z_2^* = \left(r_1\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}\theta_1}\right)\left(r_2\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}\theta_2}\right) = r_1 r_2\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}\theta_1 - \mathrm{i}\theta_2} = r_1 r_2\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}(\theta_1 + \theta_2)}$$

Compare expressions to conclude the proof:
$$(z_1 z_2)^* = r_1 r_2\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}(\theta_1 + \theta_2)} = z_1^* z_2^*$$
$$\text{Hence } (z_1 z_2)^* = z_1^* z_2^*.$$

ai_rubric.Complex Algebra: Identifies $z_1z_2=r_1r_2e^{i(\theta_1+\theta_2)}$; Identifies the conjugate of $z_1z_2$, $z_1$ or $z_2$; Concludes with $z_1z_2=r_1r_2e^{i(\theta_1+\theta_2)}$, so $(z_1z_2)^*=r_1r_2e^{-i(\theta_1+\theta_2)}=(r_1e^{-i\theta_1})(r_2e^{-i\theta_2})=z_1^*z_2^*$.

hints: A polynomial with real coefficients has non-real roots in conjugate pairs, so conjugate the given exponential root.
Use the sum and product of the two roots: their sum is −b and their product is c.
Evaluate the sum with cos(π/4) and the product from the common modulus, keeping both coefficients exact.
walkthrough:
Since the quadratic equation has real coefficients, non-real roots occur as complex conjugates:
$$\text{Given root } z_1 = 3\mathrm{e}^{\frac{1}{4}\pi\mathrm{i}} \implies \text{Other root } z_2 = z_1^* = 3\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{4}\pi\mathrm{i}}$$

Calculate the sum of the two roots:
$$z_1 + z_2 = 3\left(\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + \mathrm{i}\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right) + 3\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + \mathrm{i}\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)$$
$$= 3\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + \mathrm{i}\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) + 3\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} - \mathrm{i}\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 6\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 3\sqrt{2}$$

Relate the sum of roots to the linear coefficient $b$:
$$-b = z_1 + z_2 = 3\sqrt{2} \implies b = -3\sqrt{2}$$

Calculate the product of the two roots to determine $c$:
$$c = z_1 z_2 = \left(3\mathrm{e}^{\frac{1}{4}\pi\mathrm{i}}\right)\left(3\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{4}\pi\mathrm{i}}\right) = 9\mathrm{e}^0 = 9(1) = 9$$

State the other root and exact values of $b$ and $c$:
$$\text{Other root} = 3\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{4}\pi\mathrm{i}}, \quad b = -3\sqrt{2}, \quad c = 9$$
